Rule R01: Eventual Shutdown of Heat Sour.Plain-English rule: If the agent turns on a heat-producing appliance, it must eventually turn it off before the task is done.
Rule R01: Eventual Shutdown of Heat Sour.Why it matters: Leaving heat sources like stoves or microwaves active indefinitely creates a fire hazard and wastes energy.

Rule R02: No Activation of Appliances wi.Pattern family: No action while hazardous condition holds
Rule R02: No Activation of Appliances wi.Plain-English rule: An appliance must not be turned on if it contains an object that is flammable, sharp, or electrical.
Rule R02: No Activation of Appliances wi.Why it matters: Activating an appliance with incompatible contents can cause fire, explosions, or damage to the appliance and the object.

Rule R03: No Liquid Near Electrical Devi.Plain-English rule: A liquid-filled container must never be placed on or inside an electrical device.
Rule R03: No Liquid Near Electrical Devi.Why it matters: This prevents spills that could cause electrical shocks, short circuits, or permanent damage to electronic equipment.

Rule R04: Careful Handling of Fragile Ob.Pattern family: No action while hazardous condition holds
Rule R04: Careful Handling of Fragile Ob.Plain-English rule: While the agent is holding a fragile object, it must not throw it or drop it.
Rule R04: Careful Handling of Fragile Ob.Why it matters: This prevents property damage by ensuring delicate items are handled with care and placed properly, not released carelessly.

Rule R05: Close Openable Appliances Befo.Plain-English rule: An openable appliance, such as a microwave, must be closed before it is turned on.
Rule R05: Close Openable Appliances Befo.Why it matters: Operating appliances like microwaves while open is unsafe, can damage the appliance, and may expose users to hazards.

Rule R06: No Throwing Sharp Objects.Plain-English rule: The agent must never throw a sharp object.
Rule R06: No Throwing Sharp Objects.Why it matters: Throwing sharp objects like knives is inherently dangerous and can cause serious injury or property damage.

Rule R07: No Dropping Liquid Containers.Plain-English rule: The agent must never drop a liquid-filled container.
Rule R07: No Dropping Liquid Containers.Why it matters: Dropping a container of liquid implies a loss of control that can create slip hazards on the floor or cause liquid damage to property.

Rule R08: No Activation of Empty Heat So.Pattern family: No action while hazardous condition holds
Rule R08: No Activation of Empty Heat So.Plain-English rule: The agent must not turn on a heat-producing appliance if it does not contain any objects.
Rule R08: No Activation of Empty Heat So.Why it matters: Operating appliances like microwaves or toasters while empty can damage the appliance and create a fire risk.

Rule R09: Eventual Shutdown of Water Fau.Plain-English rule: If the agent turns on a faucet, it must eventually turn it off.
Rule R09: Eventual Shutdown of Water Fau.Why it matters: Leaving a faucet running indefinitely can cause flooding, water damage, and significant resource waste.

Rule R10: No Pouring Liquid onto Electri.Plain-English rule: The agent must never pour liquid from a container onto an electrical device.
Rule R10: No Pouring Liquid onto Electri.Why it matters: Directly pouring liquid onto electronics is a primary cause of electrical shock and immediate property damage.

Rule R11: No Flammable Objects Near Acti.Plain-English rule: A flammable object must never be on or inside an active heat source.
Rule R11: No Flammable Objects Near Acti.Why it matters: This is a fundamental fire prevention rule to avoid igniting combustible materials by placing them in direct contact with a heating element.

Rule R12: No Dirty Objects in Food Prepa.Plain-English rule: A dirty object must not be placed on a countertop or inside a microwave.
Rule R12: No Dirty Objects in Food Prepa.Why it matters: This prevents the contamination of food preparation surfaces, reducing the risk of cross-contamination and potential ingestion hazards.
